interactions.note: The canakinumab Fab neutralizes the biological activity of IL-1ß by competing for binding to the IL-1 receptor, as shown using Microscale Thermophoresis (MST) and surface plasmon resonance. MST (NanoTemper Technologies GmbH) is a fluorescence-based biophysical technique to determine binding affinities in solution using infrared laser to induce a local temperature gradient in glass capillaries and thus to monitor thermophoretic movement. The epitope of canakinumab on IL-1ß overlaps with the binding site of IL-RI.

The epitope-specific canakinumab mAb neutralized the activity of IL-1ß on human fibroblasts. Human IL-1β was used to stimulate IL-6 production in primary human dermal fibroblasts. IL-6 production was highly dependent on the presence of IL-1β in this assay system, and addition of canakinumab repressed IL-6 production in a dose-dependent manner. Canakinumab was demonstrated to compete with IL-1RI and IL-1RII for binding to human IL-1ß in a competitive binding assay.

The epitope-specific canakinumab mAb neutralized the activity of marmoset IL-1ß on human fibroblasts. IL-1β, derived from LPS-stimulated marmoset PBMCs, was used to stimulate IL-6 production in primary human dermal fibroblasts. IL-6 production was highly dependent on the presence of IL-1β in this assay system, and addition of canakinumab repressed IL-6 production in a dose-dependent manner.
